description: Every update from every ecosystem lands in one pull request on Monday morning, which CI and the end-to-end tests check like any other: Go modules, the frontend's npm packages, GitHub Actions, the OpenTofu providers, container images, the tools CI downloads, and the versions of Talos, Kubernetes, Cluster API, its providers and the add-ons that the management cluster and the clusters run. A fix for a known vulnerability comes at once, in a pull request of its own.
Renovate refuses to group a lock file refresh with other updates, so the lock files' maintenance arrives as a second pull request on Tuesday, after Monday's has had a day to be merged.
A release is offered as soon as it is published.

Renovate runs go mod tidy in a pull request that holds a major update of anything only when it also updates import paths, so gomodUpdateImportPaths is on; it rewrites imports only for a Go module's new major version.
Only node_modules is left out: config:best-practices would also skip everything under test/, and with it the image and registry the end-to-end tests run.

helm-values.description: Off. values.yaml names the Headlamp image by tag and digest alone, which this manager reads as an image called by its tag; the custom managers below read every version in it.

packageRules.description: No release waits to age, including the npm packages `config:best-practices` would otherwise hold for three days.
Go modules required only through another, which Renovate leaves alone by default, so that a fix in one of them (golang.org/x/net's, say) arrives without waiting for the module that requires it.
A major release of a Go module is a module of its own, which nothing here requires until the module that requires the old one moves; go mod tidy would take it out again.

A Kubernetes module named by a commit follows its default branch when Renovate moves it, which builds on Kubernetes' next pre-release: controller-runtime is pinned to a commit of its release-0.25 branch and moves to the next v0.25 release instead, and kube-openapi, k8s.io/utils and sigs.k8s.io/json, which publish no releases, move with the Kubernetes modules that require them.
The Prometheus operator reads the version of Prometheus and Alertmanager apart from their image and takes no digest in it; the image beside it carries the digest.
A runner image this datasource knows about is not yet a label GitHub schedules jobs on, and moving to a new image is a decision to take once, not every week.

Go, Node, Helm and kubectl publish their downloads outside GitHub, where Renovate cannot find the new SHA-256 to write beside the new version. They come in a pull request of their own so that the Monday one is not held up by a checksum taken by hand; go.mod's Go comes with them, since CI builds with the Go scripts/tools.sh installs.
prBodyNotes: Put the new SHA-256 on the line below each new version in `scripts/tools.sh`, from the checksum list published beside the download: `https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json` (`go<version>.linux-amd64.tar.gz`), `https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/SHASUMS256.txt` (`node-v<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz`), `https://get.helm.sh/helm-<tag>-linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum` and `https://dl.k8s.io/release/<tag>/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sha256`.

packageRules.description: MetalLB's chart names the FRR it is tested with, whose image Kubehenge pins beside MetalLB's.
prBodyNotes: Set `addons.metallb.values.speaker.frr.image.tag` in `charts/kubehenge/values.yaml` to the FRR tag the new chart's `values.yaml` names (`speaker.frr.image.tag`), with its digest.

packageRules.description: From v0.21.0 (chart 0.5.13) the Proxmox VE CSI plugin reads a storage's configuration through /storage/{storage}, which Proxmox VE allows only with Datastore.Allocate on the storage, the privilege that would let every cluster delete any volume on it. Clusters' tokens hold Datastore.Audit, enough for /cluster/resources, which earlier releases read; the plugin stays below until it reads the configuration that way again.
The CSI plugin's chart from 0.5.13 is made for v0.21.0, held back above.

Rancher names the versions of the webhook, Fleet, its shell and Turtles it runs with, whose images Kubehenge pins beside Rancher's; they move only with Rancher, and the Rancher test fails until they match.
prBodyNotes: Set the images under `addons.rancher` in `charts/kubehenge/values.yaml` to those of the new release, tag and digest: the webhook, Fleet and its agent, the shell and the audit log image from its `build.yaml` (`webhookVersion`, `fleetVersion`, `defaultShellVersion`, `chartAuditLogImage`), the shell three times; and `turtles` from the rancher-turtles chart `build.yaml` names (`turtlesVersion`), whose `values.yaml` names Turtles' image and whose core provider ConfigMap names the Cluster API controller's.

customManagers.description: A download from a GitHub release whose tag sits on the line above its SHA-256: the tools in scripts/tools.sh, the OpenTofu appliance/install.sh runs, the Headlamp the appliance serves, the Gateway API install file the controller carries and the cosign kubeadm templates check their images with. The tag and the digest move together; the datasource finds the new digest in the release's checksum file, or hashes the download itself.

The files the Cluster API operator installs each provider from, which the management-cluster module names by their release download's address with their SHA-256. The tag in the address and the digest move together, with the provider's version in the tested set.

Any other version named in a comment on the line above it: the tested set in the management-cluster module and its providers' images, the Talos release templates are made from, the add-on charts published as OCI images, the images the add-ons run, the images and registry the end-to-end tests run, and Go, Node, Helm and kubectl in scripts/tools.sh. An image's digest moves with its tag.

The add-on charts published in a Helm repository, which values.yaml names by repository, chart and version with the SHA-256 of its archive; the digest moves with the version, from the digest the repository's index lists.
The image ko builds Kubehenge's controller on, named by a tag that is no version, so only its digest moves.
The build of each Ubuntu release's cloud image that templates are made from, named by its directory on cloud-images.ubuntu.com, whose SHA256SUMS Ubuntu signs and Kubehenge checks.
